notes: The SSED (P250027B.pdf) and the approval order (P250027A.pdf) could be fetched, but the text is in compressed FlateDecode streams that WebFetch cannot decode. Both gave no readable text. The Read tool needs pdftoppm, which isn't installed. Bash was disabled, so I couldn't decompress the saved PDF locally. A web search confirmed the approval date (19 May 2026), the PMA filing (1 Aug 2025) and an amendment (17 Feb 2026), the 741-gene content, and the Streck tube requirement. None of the snippets named a sequencer. GenomeWeb returned HTTP 403. I did not open the FDA supplement list page or the Guardant Q2'26 transcript, so nothing is verified on the sequencer. The question of which sequencer the approved CDx names is still open.
how_to_mine: Use a shell with Python available. Decompress the saved PDF locally: C:\Users\palaz\.claude\projects\...\tool-results\webfetch-1791787078067-5tmfjb.pdf (the SSED) is already on disk. Iterate over the 'stream...endstream' blocks, run zlib.decompress on each, extract the text from the TJ/Tj operators, and grep for NovaSeq, Illumina, sequencer and instrument. Or install poppler (pdftotext) and run it on the PDF. Check the 'Device Description', 'Instruments' and 'Analytical Performance' sections, and the 'Reagents and Instruments' table. Repeat for P250027A.pdf and P250027D.pdf. If the SSED names the X, record it as the first FDA-approved test on the X and mark it 'supports' 1A. If it names the 6000 or 6000Dx, mark it 'against', because that locks the regulated volume onto the 6000. Then read the Guardant Q2'26 transcript (fool.com, 7 Aug 2026) to see whether 'completion of the NovaSeq X transition for the liquid biopsy portfolio' covers the CDx.
